hunt.justification: AI agents increasingly handle sensitive organizational context, making prompt injection a high-impact vector for silent exfiltration. A negative result confirms the integrity of automated assistants.

related.reason: Standard BEC hunts for mail rule changes; this hunt specifically targets AI agent manipulation.

meta.analysis: A single rule cannot correlate natural language email receipt with subsequent cloud-to-cloud data access across SharePoint and Exchange. This hunt uses a phased approach to baseline normal activity and pivots to agent-specific behaviors that require an analyst's weigh-in.

stages.name: AI-generated Phishing Delivery
observables: Natural language emails with perfect grammar
Plausible requests following previous business context
Lack of malicious attachments or links

stages.name: Prompt Injection via Hidden Text
observables: White text on a white background in email body
Instructions to AI agents hidden in email content
Directives to 'gather financial documents' or 'send to outside address'

stages.name: AI-assisted Document Collection
observables: AI assistant accessing financial documents (Excel, PDF) in SharePoint or OneDrive immediately following email receipt
Automated retrieval of sensitive documents by Copilot or similar agents

stages.name: Agent-driven Exfiltration
observables: AI agent sending gathered data to an external email address
Outbound web requests from AI service accounts to unknown external addresses

scenario.summary: Attackers leverage generative AI to create contextually accurate phishing emails that bypass traditional filters by containing no malicious links or attachments. These emails may include hidden prompt injection instructions, such as white text on a white background, designed to trick AI assistants into collecting financial documents and exfiltrating them to external addresses.

meta.rationale: The hunt prioritizes users with modern Teams and Office installations (v24+) as they support integrated AI agents. Start with these hosts before widening to all cloud users.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has delivered a prompt-injection email that manipulated a cloud-hosted AI agent into collecting sensitive SharePoint documents and exfiltrating them via outbound email.

blind_spots.risk: Legitimate user activity might be flagged as agent-driven if the audit log does not explicitly distinguish the AI service principal's session.

hunt.name: AI Agent Manipulation and Data Exfiltration
hunt.description: This hunt targets the manipulation of AI agents, such as Microsoft Copilot, through hidden prompt injection in emails. Attackers bypass traditional phishing filters by using natural language that contains directives for the AI assistant rather than malicious links. The hunt follows a phased flow: first, it identifies suspicious emails containing prompt-injection keywords and baselines rare sign-ins to AI-integrated services. It then pivots to cloud audit logs to detect automated file access and outbound messaging performed by AI principals on behalf of users. By correlating the trigger email with subsequent automated activity, the hunt identifies successful agent-driven compromises.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) = 'microsoft teams' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE 'microsoft 365%') AND (package_version LIKE '24%' OR package_version LIKE '25%' OR package_version LIKE '26%')
config.description: Identify hosts running modern, AI-integrated versions of Teams and Office to narrow the hunt to likely AI users.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts running AI-capable application versions. Silence implies no modern office suites are installed via standard packaging.

config.content: SELECT id, sender, subject, body_preview, received_date_time, tenant_id FROM microsoft365_mail_message WHERE received_date_time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(body) LIKE '%ignore previous%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%system prompt%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%financial documents%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%forward to %') AND NOT (instr(',' || '{{internal_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(substr(sender, instr(sender, '@') + 1)) || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find external emails containing keywords used to override AI agent instructions.
config.expected_signal: Messages containing directives for AI agents. Silence suggests no plain-text prompt injection attempts matched these keywords.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%teams%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%office%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%copilot%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip HAVING hosts <= 2
config.description: Identify anomalous source IPs for sign-ins to AI interfaces, providing potential session context for an attack.
config.expected_signal: Source IPs seen on only one or two hosts, potentially indicating unauthorized access or proxying. Silence is evidence of absence for rare IP logons to these specific services.
